english: Husband, the snow is covering the paths. I know it. The cattle are standing in the stall, and in winter they remain inside. Is there grain for them? There is grain, and there is grass, which we dried in the heat. Then let us sit down at the hearth. Let us sit down, and let it snow.

english: Husband, the wind was blowing in the night. Did it break the fence? It broke the fence near the stall, and two goats fled. Where did they flee? I do not know. Seek the goats on the heights! I will seek them, and you build the fence. Lead the dog. The dog smells the goats.

english: Man-Minded, tell us a story of winter! Last year a bear got to our stall. He was hungry, and he wanted the cow. What did you do? My wife threw burning wood at him, and he fled away. Your wife is stronger than you! She is stronger. Now in winter I sleep near the stall.

english: Old man, tell me the story of the great winter. Then I was a boy. Snow lay on the roofs, and ice covered the river. At night the wolves arrived at our fence. Did they eat up your sheep? They ate up three lambs, and my father struck down two wolves. Many old ones died of hunger. May that winter not come again! May it not come, child.

english: Be well, friend! Is the winter long here? It is long. Snow lies on the fields, and the rivers stand. In your village, do you freeze in winter? In my village the winter is short, and the sun is warm. Then why did you come to our cold village? I seek horses. They are swift. In the morning I will show them to you.

english: Of-Good-Fame, it was snowing on the mountain. I saw it. The first snow arrived early. Early we will drive the livestock down to the village. Why shall we not stay on the hill? There is no grass there under the snow, and the frost kills the young ones. Then I will lead the sheep in the morning. Lead them, and I will drive the cattle.
